- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.

# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Overview

The Green Party's 2024 manifesto addresses the cost of living crisis, climate emergency, and public service decline. It proposes significant public investment funded through wealth taxation and borrowing.

## Health and Social Care

The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS spending by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, ensuring NHS dentist availability for all, boosting staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. The party opposes NHS privatisation and supports the NHS Reinstatement Bill.

For social care, the manifesto proposes £20bn annual investment, free personal care, improved pay and career structures for carers, and increased disability benefits by 5%.

## Housing

The manifesto targets 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering local authorities to introduce rent controls, and ending no-fault evictions. A home retrofit programme would invest £29bn over five years for insulation and £9bn for heating systems.

## Energy and Climate

The party proposes no new oil and gas licences, ending fossil fuel subsidies, and introducing a carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne. Wind power would provide approximately 70% of electricity by 2030. The manifesto supports community energy ownership and opposes nuclear power development.

## Economy and Public Finances

Average annual green investment of £40bn is proposed, covering electricity generation, building retrofits, railways, and public transport. Railways, water companies, and major retail energy companies would return to public ownership.

Revenue measures include a wealth tax (1% on assets above £10m, 2% above £1bn), aligning capital gains tax with income tax rates, and reforming inheritance tax. The party estimates these could raise £50-70bn annually by parliament's end.

## Work and Welfare

Proposals include a £15 minimum wage for all ages, maximum 10:1 pay ratios, repealing anti-union legislation, and moving toward a four-day working week. Universal Credit would increase by £40 weekly, the two-child benefit cap would be abolished, and the five-week benefit wait would end.

## Education

The manifesto proposes £8bn additional school funding, £2.5bn annually for building repairs, scrapping tuition fees, restoring maintenance grants, and £5bn for special educational needs provision. Academies would return to local authority control.

## Transport

Annual public transport subsidies would reach £10bn, with railways returning to public ownership. Investment of £2.5bn annually would support cycling and walking infrastructure. The manifesto proposes ending petrol and diesel vehicle sales by 2027 and opposing new road building.

## Environment and Nature

A Rights of Nature Act would give nature legal personhood. The target is 30% of land and sea protected by 2030. Water companies would return to public ownership. Additional measures include a Right to Roam Act and £1.5bn increase to DEFRA's budget.

## Food and Farming

Farm support would nearly triple over five years to support nature-friendly farming transition. Proposals include free school meals for all children, reducing pesticide use, and increasing domestic food production.

## Democracy and Rights

The manifesto proposes replacing first-past-the-post with proportional representation, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, and repealing the Elections Act 2022. The party supports continued membership of the European Convention on Human Rights.

## Immigration

Proposals include ending the hostile environment policy, removing minimum income requirements for spousal visas, establishing safe asylum routes, and permitting asylum seekers to work during application processing.

## International Affairs

The party supports an immediate bilateral ceasefire in Gaza, recognising Palestine, ending UK arms exports to Israel, rejoining the EU, and signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons while cancelling Trident. Overseas aid would increase to 1% of GNI by 2033.

## Funding

The manifesto projects revenue spending reaching £161.6bn by 2030 and capital spending of £90.3bn. Taxation measures would raise £172.4bn by 2030, with remaining costs funded through borrowing.
